The hyperbola $x^2-\frac{y^2}{3}=1$ has $a=1$, $b=\sqrt{3}$, $c=2$, so $F_1=(-2,0)$, $F_2=(2,0)$ and $F_1F_2=4$.

For $A=(x_A,y_A)$ on the right branch, $AF_1=2x_A+1$, $AF_2=2x_A-1$. The semiperimeter of $\triangle AF_1F_2$ is $s=\frac{(2x_A+1)+(2x_A-1)+4}{2}=2x_A+2$, and its area is $\frac12\cdot 4\cdot|y_A|=2|y_A|$. Hence the inradius is
$$r_A=\frac{2|y_A|}{2x_A+2}=\frac{|y_A|}{x_A+1}=\sqrt{3}\sqrt{\frac{x_A-1}{x_A+1}}.$$
Set $u_A=\sqrt{\frac{x_A-1}{x_A+1}}$ (so $r_A=\sqrt3\,u_A$) and similarly $u_B$ for $B$. Collinearity of $A,B,F_2$ yields the relation
$$\frac{y_A}{x_A-2}=\frac{y_B}{x_B-2}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u_Au_B=\frac13.$$
A line through $F_2$ meets the right branch in two points exactly when its slope satisfies $|k|>\sqrt3$ (including the vertical line). This forces $u_A,u_B\in(\tfrac13,1)$ with $u_Au_B=\tfrac13$, so writing $u_B=\frac{1}{3u_A}$ we have $u_A\in[\frac1{\sqrt3},1)$ and
$$u_A+u_B=u_A+\frac{1}{3u_A}$$
which is minimized at $u_A=\frac1{\sqrt3}$ (the vertical chord, $x=2$) giving $\frac{2}{\sqrt3}$, and increases to the supremum $1+\frac13=\frac43$ as one endpoint tends to infinity (the line approaching an asymptote).

Therefore $r_A+r_B=\sqrt3\,(u_A+u_B)$ ranges from $\sqrt3\cdot\frac{2}{\sqrt3}=2$ up to (but not including) $\sqrt3\cdot\frac43=\frac{4\sqrt3}{3}$.
